record.paper_title: On a general Syracuse problem with conjectures
record.context_brief: Finiteness and basin decomposition for generalized Syracuse maps
record.original_question: Let a and b be odd integers with a > −b and a + b = 2^ν₀ for some integer ν₀ ≥ 1. Define T on positive integers by T(n)=n/2 when n is even and T(n)=(a n+b)/2 when n is odd. A cycle is a finite orbit Ω with T^k(x)=x for every x in Ω; C(a,b) is the set of all cycles. For a cycle Ω(ω) whose smallest element is ω, let G(ω) be the set of starting values that eventually reach ω, and let G(∞) be the set of starting values whose iterates diverge to infinity. Is C(a,b) always finite, with the positive integers decomposing as the union of the finitely many cycle basins G(ω₁*), …, G(ω_q*) and the possible divergent set G(∞)?

evidence.quote: We consider the map T : N − → N given by T (n) = { n/ 2 if n is even , (an + b)/ 2 if n is odd , (2) where a and b are both odd integers such that a > − b.

A cycle of the graph associated to the map T having k vertices is a trajectory Ω for which T (k)(x) = x for all x ∈ Ω. The cardinal #Ω = Card (Ω) = k, also called the length, of Ω is in fact the smallest integer such that T (k)(x) = x for all x ∈ Ω.
G(ω ) = { n ∈ N : ∃ k ∈ N, T (k)(n) = ω } , and G(∞ ) = { n ∈ N : lim k→∞ T (k)(n) = ∞} .

Conjecture 2.1. For any parameters a and b such that a + b = 2 ν 0, where ν 0 ≥ 1, the set C(a, b ) has ﬁnite cardinality: 1 ≤ q∗ = # C(a, b ) < ∞ . Then, it follows that there is q∗ distinct integers ω ∗ 1, . . . , ω ∗ q∗ such that: C(a, b ) = { Ω(ω ∗ 1), . . . , Ω(ω ∗ q∗) } , and N = G(ω ∗ 1) ∪ · · · ∪ G(ω ∗ q∗ ) ∪ G(∞ ). The set G(∞ ) may be empty or not empty.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $a$ and $b$ be odd integers satisfying $a > -b$ and $a + b = 2^{\nu_0}$ for some integer $\nu_0 \geq 1$. Define a map $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ on the positive integers by
$$T(n) = \begin{cases} n/2 & \text{if } n \text{ is even},\\ (an+b)/2 & \text{if } n \text{ is odd}, \end{cases}$$
(assume the parameters are chosen so that $T(\mathbb{N}) \subseteq \mathbb{N}$). A cycle of $T$ is a finite nonempty set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{N}$ together with an integer $k \geq 1$ such that $T^{(k)}(x) = x$ for every $x \in \Omega$; the length of $\Omega$ is the smallest such $k$. Denote by $\mathcal{C}(a,b)$ the collection of all cycles of $T$. For a cycle $\Omega$ with smallest element $\omega$, define its basin
$$G(\omega) = \{ n \in \mathbb{N} : \exists\, k \in \mathbb{N},\ T^{(k)}(n) = \omega \},$$
and the divergent set
$$G(\infty) = \{ n \in \mathbb{N} : \lim_{k \to \infty} T^{(k)}(n) = \infty \}.$$
Prove or disprove: for every admissible pair $(a,b)$ as above, $\mathcal{C}(a,b)$ is finite, say $\mathcal{C}(a,b) = \{\Omega(\omega_1^*), \ldots, \Omega(\omega_{q^*}^*)\}$ with $1 \leq q^* < \infty$, and
$$\mathbb{N} = G(\omega_1^*) \cup \cdots \cup G(\omega_{q^*}^*) \cup G(\infty),$$
where $G(\infty)$ may or may not be empty.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a generalization of the Collatz (3x+1) problem to a family of affine maps $T(n) = (an+b)/2$ on odd inputs. The classical Collatz conjecture (the case $a=3$, $b=1$) remains famously open; analogous finiteness-of-cycles and basin-decomposition statements for generalized Syracuse maps are widely conjectured but unproven. Tao (2019) showed that almost all Collatz orbits attain almost bounded values, but the full conjecture, including the absence of divergent orbits and finiteness of cycles, is open. No proof of the stated general conjecture is known.

status_evidence.title: Almost all orbits of the Collatz map attain almost bounded values (Tao)
status_evidence.snippet: We show that for any function f tending to infinity, almost all Collatz orbits attain a value below f(n); the full conjecture remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The classical 3x+1 Collatz problem (a special case) is still open, only partial probabilistic results exist.

status_evidence.title: The 3x+1 problem: An overview (Lagarias)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the 3x+1 problem and its generalizations, noting that finiteness of cycles and trivial dynamics conjectures remain unresolved in general.
status_evidence.claim: Generalized Syracuse/Collatz conjectures on finite cycle sets and basin decompositions are open.
